policy_title: Build Two Carbon Capture and Storage Clusters
stated: The Conservative Party will build the first two carbon capture and storage clusters across North Wales, the North West of England, Teesside, and the Humber, creating jobs and cutting carbon, while progressing a second tranche of projects.

source.quote: Build the first two carbon capture and storage clusters, based across North Wales and, the North West of England and Teesside and the Humber, cutting carbon and creating tens of thousands of jobs in these regions, and progress the second tranche of projects in Aberdeenshire and the Humber.

bearing_set.reason: CCS clusters directly target carbon emissions reduction, bearing materially on emissions trajectory and climate outcomes.
Policy explicitly claims job creation in named industrial regions (Teesside, Humber, North West, North Wales), warranting a real verdict on employment quality and quantity.
Building major industrial CCS clusters involves significant capital investment and job creation in specific regions, materially affecting aggregate economic opportunity and regional living standards.

CCS clusters of this scale require substantial public subsidy (capital and revenue support contracts worth billions, as seen with Track-1/2 programmes), materially affecting the funded vs borrowed spending balance.

The specific geographic targeting — Teesside, Humber, North Wales, North West — places economic activity in historically left-behind, higher-deprivation regions, bearing concretely on regional inequality indicators.

membership_note: Policy has two explicitly stated aims (carbon reduction and job creation) plus a large implicit fiscal commitment, justifying four bearings: the environmental mechanism (O6), aggregate economic/opportunity effect (O13), public finance cost (O12), and regional inequality effect of deliberate geographic targeting (O14).
